NTT operates a global data center business, NTT Global Data Centers, under NTT DATA, Inc. The operators own about us page, fetched this session, states NTT DATA is a top 10 global IT services provider with about 30 billion dollars in annual revenue, operations across 33 countries, and about 3 billion dollars in annual research and development investment, headquartered at the Toyosu Center Building, 3-3-3 Toyosu, Koto-ku, Tokyo 135-6033, Japan, though these figures describe the wider NTT DATA organization rather than the data center division specifically, and no data center division formation or acquisition date was found on the pages fetched this session. A previously confirmed, specific data center acquisition remains NTT Communications purchase of an 86.7 percent stake in e-shelter, described as Germany top data center operator, completed around June 23, 2015, though that acquisition is not directly connected to this United States facility. This session reached the operators own services.global.ntt data center locations pages directly and successfully. An earlier sessions attempts to reach the ragingwire.com domain had failed and found no corresponding Wikipedia article, a negative finding this session did not need to repeat. This session found and fetched the operators own dedicated CH2 facility page directly, giving 275 Pierce Rd, Itasca, IL 60143, 36 MW of critical IT load, and about 126,000 square feet of IT space. A reverse geocode of this rows own coordinates, tried first, returned a single candidate on a different street entirely at a wide distance, and was set aside once the operators own dedicated page gave a clear, directly on point answer instead. The operators own current Chicago area locations overview page, also fetched this session, independently names CH1, CH2, and CH3 as active facilities on a campus with a planned 200 plus MW of IT load once fully built out, corroborating CH2 as a real, current facility.

reading.body:
NTT Chicago CH2 is a 36 MW facility in Itasca, Illinois, confirmed by the operator's published specifications. At an assumed 40 kW per rack, this capacity represents roughly 900 racks of IT equipment across 126,000 square feet of technical space. The facility is part of a multi-building campus on Pierce Road that the operator has announced will reach 200 MW or more of IT load once fully built out, making it one component of a significantly larger infrastructure project underway in the Chicago area.

Illinois has published capacity totaling 236 MW across six facilities with confirmed specifications from operator sources. NTT Chicago CH2 ranks seventh by published megawatts in the state, placing it below the current published leaders but within a small set of quantified capacity at a time when most of the 44 mapped facilities in Illinois publish no figures. The state context does not indicate how Chicago CH2's capacity compares to the full buildout announced for the campus or to typical data center deployments serving AI workloads.

The facility's scale and operator assignment make it relevant to track as AI deployment patterns emerge. NTT is one of the world's largest telecommunications and IT services providers, with a global data center business. No information is published about which tenants occupy NTT Chicago CH2, the power supply route, or whether grid constraints currently affect its operation or expansion plans.
